ablations.label: v7 with the v6 HHI convention
ablations.note: v6 always added the squared residual, which is the v7 upper bound — so this is unchanged from base and confirms the HHI change moved no headline number, only the published interval.

ablations.label: v7 with the lower HHI bound
ablations.note: The optimistic completion of the unobserved residual. Affects structural scores, not the operational field.

ablations.label: v7 with max incident aggregation
ablations.note: Only the single largest incident counts per stage. Isolates how much of the headline number is cumulative rather than dominant.

ablations.label: v7 with clipped-sum incident aggregation
ablations.note: Fully additive up to the bound. The upper end of the aggregation model form.

ablations.label: v7 with equal stage weighting
ablations.note: Drops the turnover proxy entirely from the headline weighting.

ablations.label: v7 with log-turnover stage weighting
ablations.note: Compresses the turnover skew; closest to the v6 max-normalized log1p weighting, which did NOT sum to one.

ablations.label: v7 with a 12-day market half-life (the single v6 half-life)
ablations.note: The nearest v7 setting to v6's single 12-day half-life for every event class. Isolates most of the headline movement: v6 decayed policy, allocation and pricing incidents as fast as a fab inspection.

materialChangesByCause.change: Event-specific persistence replaces one global 12-day half-life
materialChangesByCause.why: v6 decayed every incident class at the same 12-day half-life, so a standing export-control regime and a same-week fab inspection faded identically and almost everything older than a quarter contributed nothing. v7 gives allocation, pricing and licensing incidents a market half-life (base 45 d), outages a staged linear recovery, and standing controls a dated in-force window. More of the recorded operational history is therefore live at the snapshot date. This is the single largest contributor to the headline movement — see the 12-day ablation.
materialChangesByCause.evidence: ablations["v7 with a 12-day market half-life (the single v6 half-life)"]

materialChangesByCause.direction: lowers the field at broadly tagged incidents
materialChangesByCause.why: v6 propagated each of an incident's tagged stages separately, each carrying the incident's FULL severity, then combined the results with a noisy-OR — so tagging one earthquake to four stages injected four full-severity shocks. v7 builds one source vector for the incident, with a per-stage exposure alpha in [0,1], and propagates it jointly. A record tagged to more stages now spreads its severity rather than multiplying it.

materialChangesByCause.change: Joint incident propagation replaces per-stage noisy-OR combination
materialChangesByCause.why: Within one incident, two paths that reconverge on a stage are the same disruption arriving twice. v6 combined them as if independent, which added an interaction term with nothing to represent. v7 sums the dependency-weighted inflows and clips once.

materialChangesByCause.direction: lowers country readings for countries tagged on incidents they also host stages for
materialChangesByCause.why: v6 combined a country-tagged incident's raw magnitude into the country reading ON TOP of the same incident's stage field, so such an incident counted twice. In v7 an incident reaches a country only through its stage source and propagation.

materialChangesByCause.change: Continuous facility exposure replaces the 5% scoring threshold
materialChangesByCause.direction: lowers large hazard deltas, raises small ones
materialChangesByCause.why: v6 gave a 5.01% footprint the same full-severity shock as a 100% footprint and gave a 4.99% footprint nothing at all. v7 scales the source by the footprint share, so broad shallow radii shrink and narrow marginal ones become visible instead of vanishing.

materialChangesByCause.change: Policy exposure is deduplicated into families and aggregated with a bounded operator
materialChangesByCause.direction: lowers policy exposure where a stage was covered by several register rows
materialChangesByCause.why: v6 used "strongest + 0.4 x the sum of the rest" over RECORDS, which grew without bound in the number of rows and rose when the same control was re-reported. v7 collapses records into policy families, takes the strongest reading within a family, and combines families with a bounded operator that saturates at 10.

materialChangesByCause.change: Stage economic weights are normalized to sum to one
materialChangesByCause.direction: changes the headline weighting AND every weight-derived measure — network influence moves the most of any published number
materialChangesByCause.why: v6 weighted by a MAX-normalized log1p transform, so the weights summed to an arbitrary number and the headline index was a weighted mean with a hand-shaped denominator. v7 normalizes turnover directly to a partition of one, which is what makes the country chain contributions reconcile to the headline index exactly. The log1p transform also compressed the turnover range hard: a 500B stage and a 3B stage differed by about 2.5x in v6 weight and by about 170x in v7. Network influence sums the propagated field against these weights, so it re-ranks accordingly, and structural vulnerability moves with it. This is a change in the WEIGHTING, not in any stage field: the operational field per stage is unaffected by it.

materialChangesByCause.change: HHI is published as an interval
materialChangesByCause.direction: no change to the published base score
materialChangesByCause.why: v6 silently used what v7 calls the UPPER bound (residual treated as one undisclosed holder). v7 publishes that as the explicitly conservative base and publishes the lower bound beside it, and includes the choice in sensitivity. The base number is unchanged; what changed is that the reader can now see it is one end of an interval.

materialChangesByCause.change: Relative scores are labelled as snapshot-relative and published beside their raw values
materialChangesByCause.direction: no numerical change to the relative scores
materialChangesByCause.why: Network influence and company criticality are divided by the largest value in the CURRENT snapshot, so they order things within one snapshot and are not comparable across snapshots. v6 published only the rescaled number. v7 publishes the raw measure too, so a reader can compare across snapshots using something that means the same thing twice.

materialChangesByCause.change: Company criticality no longer applies topology twice
materialChangesByCause.direction: reorders companies whose stages differ in connectivity
materialChangesByCause.why: v6 propagated a company's disruption across the graph and then weighted the resulting field by NETWORK_INFLUENCE, which is itself a propagation-derived reachability measure. A company on a well-connected stage was rewarded twice for the same connectivity. v7 weights by the economic weight, which carries no topology.

causes: Continuous exposure scaling: v6 shocked every stage above the 5% footprint line at FULL severity and every stage below it at zero; v7 scales each stage source by its footprint share, so a broad radius now produces many small sources instead of a few maximal ones.
Below-threshold stages now score: stages v6 discarded entirely contribute in proportion to their footprint.
Multi-stage full-shock multiplication removed: v6 injected the scenario severity independently at every material stage; v7 injects one source vector for the whole hazard.

Continuous exposure scaling: v6 shocked every stage above the 5% footprint line at FULL severity and every stage below it at zero; v7 scales each stage source by its footprint share, so a broad radius now produces many small sources instead of a few maximal ones.
